deployments.how: Size of this phase: 218 MW facility; estimated: IT x PUE 1.3. This row: 218 MW energising in 2026-Q4 (timing estimated: all MW placed at first power (no full-capacity date)). Chip maker google: estimated. Estimate: Google TPU, Ironwood generation for 2026 deliveries. Reasoning: Google guarantees Fluidstack's lease here; Fluidstack builds Anthropic's own US capacity (Texas, New York); Anthropic contracted up to one million Google TPUs with well over 1 GW online in 2026. A Google-backstopped Fluidstack hall serving Anthropic most plausibly holds TPUs. Fluidstack also runs NVIDIA clusters, so NVIDIA is the alternative. No source states the chip. Operator is an estimate: No operator is named in a source. Fluidstack leases this capacity and runs its own cloud in it, so it is taken to run the facility. This may change when a tenant or operator is announced. End user is an estimate: Estimate: end customer Anthropic. Anthropic said its $50bn Fluidstack build is in Texas and New York; Fluidstack's Google-backstopped US leases are the candidates, but no source ties this building to Anthropic by name.

This row is the part of the agreement that is not yet at a named site: 910 MW of 910 MW. Location as stated, at country level only. Finland: Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala. deployments.how: Size of this phase: 150 MW facility; stated gross. Region launch with no size: method c with 3 buildings (multiple availability zones; three assumed as for other new AWS regions) x 50 MW = 150 MW facility (Estimate). Adjusted in review: The whole estimated region size was placed in the launch month. A region does not open at full size, so the size is kept and spread over three years. This row: 18 MW energising in 2026-Q1 (timing estimated) This is 12% of the phase. Estimate. A new cloud region opens with a first set of halls and fills over the following years. One third of the estimated 150 MW is placed in the launch month and one third in each of the next two years. Chip maker amazon: estimated. 78 MW is shown under nvidia because the buyer's agreement 'Nvidia to supply about one million AI processors to AWS by end-2027' has no site named and is assumed to be housed in its sites with no chip on record. The allocation to this site is an estimate. 72 MW with no chip on record is shown under amazon, nvidia as an estimate: AWS deploys its own Trainium chips and Nvidia GPUs; shared by the size of its Trainium and Nvidia agreements. End user is an estimate: Self-operated public cloud; operator taken as end user (Estimate).

deals.name: Microsoft company-wide capacity additions, FY2025 to 2032 (stated quarterly adds, "double in two years", reported ~38 GW by 2032)

estimated.capacity_mw: Estimate. Total fleet about 38 GW by 2032 (press report, source 7) minus an estimated base of about 5.5 GW on 1 July 2024. Base = about 12 GW in Sept 2026 (source 7) minus the 6.52 GW added from Jul 2024 to Sep 2026 (schedule below). 38,000 - 5,480 = 32,520, rounded to 32,500. Basis of Microsoft's "capacity" (IT or power) is not given; treated as facility.
estimated.schedule: Quarterly increments, Microsoft fiscal quarters mapped to calendar quarters. Stated by Microsoft: FY25 (Jul 2024 to Jun 2025) "more than two gigawatts" (source 1); Oct-Dec 2025 "nearly one gigawatt" (source 3, taken as 1,000); Jan-Mar 2026 "another gigawatt" (source 4); Apr-Jun 2026 "another gigawatt" (source 5). Estimates: Jul-Dec 2024 = half of FY25 (1,000); Jul-Sep 2025 = 750 (between the FY25 average of 500 per quarter and the ~1,000 per quarter that followed; Microsoft gave no GW figure, source 2); Jul-Sep 2026 = 770 (24 datacenters added, source 6, scaled by the 1 GW that 31 datacenters brought in Apr-Jun 2026, source 5). 2027-Q3 = Microsoft's statement that it will "roughly double" total capacity in two years from Oct 2025 (sources 2, 4, 5): fleet at Sep 2025 about 8.23 GW (5.48 base + 2.75 added), doubled = 16.46 GW, i.e. 10,980 MW added since Jul 2024. Oct-Dec 2026 and Oct-Dec 2027 take the straight-line quarterly pace of the neighbouring segment (1,115 and 1,025 MW). 2028-2032: straight line from 12,000 at end-2027 to 32,500 at end-2032 (4,100 MW a year), the reported 38 GW endpoint (source 7). Lease evidence that the build continues past 2027: 364.6bn USD of leases signed but not yet commenced at 30 Sep 2026, commencing FY2027 to FY2034 (source 9; 329.1bn at 30 Jun 2026 commencing FY2027 to FY2033, source 8).

deals.notes: Company-level capacity that Microsoft has added or plans to add since 1 July 2024, all regions, owned, leased and third-party. Microsoft's own statements: more than 2 GW added in FY2025; nearly 1 GW (Oct-Dec 2025), 1 GW (Jan-Mar 2026) and 1 GW (Apr-Jun 2026) a quarter; 88 datacenters added in FY2026 and 24 in Jul-Sep 2026; "roughly double" total capacity in two years (Oct 2025, repeated Apr and Jul 2026); AI capacity to rise by over 80% in FY2026 (Oct 2025 call, paraphrase). The 2032 endpoint (about 12 GW in Sept 2026 to about 38 GW by 2032) is a Bloomberg report of an internal plan that Microsoft has not confirmed. Money: capex FY2026 145.3bn USD (Q1 34.9, Q2 37.5, Q3 31.9, Q4 41.0), finance leases commenced 11.1bn (Q1 FY26), 6.7bn (Q2), 4.7bn (Q3), 5.6bn (Q4) and 7.4bn (Q1 FY27); capex Q1 FY27 45.2bn; calendar 2026 capex guided at about 190bn (Apr 2026), then about 170bn (Oct 2026) after third-party capacity deliveries slipped into H2 FY27. Leases signed but not commenced: 329.1bn USD at 30 Jun 2026 (FY2027 to FY2033) and 364.6bn USD at 30 Sep 2026 (FY2027 to FY2034), terms 1 to 20 years; 10-K lease commitments 32.41bn for FY2027 and 411.1bn after (DCD). Microsoft says Azure Maia will scale to multi-gigawatt deployments from 2027 (blogs.microsoft.com, 2026-10-12). This record overlaps every Microsoft site and neocloud contract;
